| [ADR-030](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-030.md) | Every practice states its origin, even when it is the primary source | [ADR-029](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-029.md) made `introduced_by:` optional and set a condition for promotion: a pass over the practices should find origins that differ from the primary source often enough for the field to carry information. The field is required anyway, for a reason that condition did not test — an absent field was ambiguous between "the origin is the primary source" and "nobody checked", and those are different claims. | [ADR-031](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-031.md) | A scheme for explanations, complementing the practice registry | A third scheme, THEORY, for claims about WHY something works. A THEORY names its `source:` like a practice does, and `explains:` the practices it underwrites, which the practices read back as `explained_by:`. | [ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md) | Advice on how to prove a theorem is out of scope; advice on how to find out whether a technique worked is not | Six recommendations in the [#139](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/issues/139) import tell a reader how to construct a proof — use the bounded-Lipschitz metric, check a log-Sobolev inequality, work in a rigged Hilbert space. It is right, and the reason is the scope test in [ADR-026](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-026.md): the reader this anthology addresses is training a model. The test: strip the algorithm's name from the sentence and see whether anything is left to do. | Proposed |

Rejected: a status below `Proposed`, and parking the doubt in `consensus`. | Proposed |
| [ADR-045](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-045.md) | A claim about the signal is admissible however it was measured, including on people | A psycholinguistics paper arrived with a real measurement, no model and no recommendation, and the first instinct was to file it as a LIT note that sources nothing — admitted on an exception. That was wrong twice over: the record already holds physics, control theory and pure mathematics, so "outside CS" was never the boundary; and the paper's finding is a claim about what is TRUE, which is what THEORY holds. Proposed: the scheme follows the kind of claim, not the apparatus that produced it, so a finding about the signal is a THEORY whether it was measured on a GPU or on 755 people — provided its document says what it does not license. Rejected: the exception framing, sourcing a practice from it, and adding a topic. | Proposed |

| [ADR-053](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-053.md) | A practice may state that it has no identifiable origin, by leaving introduced_by empty | [ADR-030](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-030.md) made `introduced_by:` required because an absent field was ambiguous between "the origin is the primary source" and "nobody checked". Write the field explicitly empty, with a comment saying what was searched, and the emptiness is a claim a reader can falsify by naming the paper.
